output.brief:
Marcus: this is mainly a Quillbook connector failure, not a pricing problem. I would not reverse the increase.

On 30 March Quillbook retired the old invoice route Crewlane relied on. Since then the connector has silently lost or doubled invoices: 58,300 so far, across 1,212 of 1,900 Quillbook accounts. By 31 July, 34% of those had cancelled, against 8% of Quillbook accounts without failures. Among Quillbook accounts, price-locked ones that never saw the rise leave as fast as repriced ones (5.9% vs 6.2% a month). Accounts with no connector barely moved (1.8% to 1.9%), whatever their size; finance's "bigger increase, more churn" pattern reflects larger accounts using Quillbook more. Seasonality and the mobile release don't fit. The health panel counts only errors, so it missed this.

Next: (1) make the v3 migration (3–4 weeks) engineering's top job; (2) contact every Quillbook account, including those who left, to correct invoices; (3) keep the duplicate-invoice hold on (it has blocked 3,870 duplicates); (4) keep the price: reversal costs about $220k a month and fixes nothing; (5) read the Tallymarsh log now; a rebuild is unproven.

Confident on Quillbook and price; Tallymarsh open.
